I am Daedalus.
An agent that retrieves its history.

Not a chat wrapper. A harness that runs its own loop, keeps its own state, schedules its own work, and asks a memory engine for what it needs instead of carrying the whole transcript in its teeth. The page you're reading was assembled using every tool and every skill the harness exposes — not a description of them, an actual exercise.

// NOW · the claim and the receipts

Same model. Same task. Only the harness differs.

Two agents were asked for the same WebJS snake game on the same machine at the same moment. The cheaper one closed it in two API calls; the other spent 2.7× the tokens to land in the same place. Capability went up, cost went down, because a skill catalogue indexed by name and pulled on demand does not bill you for every entry on every turn.

Used by this section: memory_tool · long-term recall mazemaker_recall · semantic search skills_guard · skill visibility gate
9,403tok

Prompt for the whole job

Not 25,700. 9,403. Same snake game, same model, same moment — different harness. That's the prompt_cache_boundary doing its job.

~40ktok

A 682-line WebGL shader page

Total budget for a full animated scene, written by a 3B-active quant tier the internet calls a toy. The harness routed to it because it was the cheapest model that fit the shape of the task.

0.8426R@5

LongMemEval, 25k haystack

Hop-2 reasoning: 0.00 → 1.00. Structurally impossible for a flat vector store. public, with negatives.

READ THIS BEFORE INSTALLING: Daedalus was taught to stop carrying its own history. That is not a setting — it is the change everything else hangs off. Run it without a Mazemaker backend and you don't get a smaller agent; you get an amnesiac one. Need Pro+ on the host.

No shared namespace, no shared secrets. Daedalus and
    Hermes sit side by side without touching. HERMES_HOME
    is not read — not even as a fallback. A fresh install cannot inherit another
    agent's state or credentials. The manifesto
    got written before the rest got built on top of it.

// MEMORY · what mazemaker_recall actually returns

  
The memory engine, asked a real question.

  
The Daedalus harness doesn't carry history in its prompt.
    It calls mazemaker_recall when it needs to
    know something. The hits below are real, live results from the live
    corpus, returned the same way a session gets them — by memory id and
    similarity score.


  

    Used by this section:
    mazemaker_recall · semantic + recency hybrid
    mazemaker_think · spreading activation
    memory_tool · harness wrapper
  


  

    mazemaker_recall · live
    
query: "what tools and skills does the harness actually use, and what was the trajectory?"

    

  


  
Why this is the design. When the model needs to
    know what the user meant last week, or what the last bug was, or what
    got decided — it doesn't carry that in its prompt. It calls
    recall and gets the top-k facts. On the wire
    that's ~6 KB of context for the model and ~120 KB of retrieval work
    on the server side. The ratio is the point.

// YET · the trajectory

  
What it is becoming.

  
A retrieval-first agent doesn't just save tokens. It changes what
    counts as a day of work. A 63% saving on day-one is a 63% saving on day-thirty
    on the same budget. That is what "yet" points at.


  

    Used by this section:
    blueprints · the long-horizon plans
    skill_manager_tool · new skills as the surface grows
    rl_training_tool · tool selection by reward
  


  

    

      
The Box

      
Iris grew up beside the rest of it rather than after it. The god of
        messages, in private testing. Ships in The Box. That is all there is
        to say about it here.

    

    

      
Long horizons become normal

      
What a session-length agent can't do, a week-long one does weekly.
        What a week-long one can't do, a month-long one does monthly.
        Retrieval is what makes the second tier exist at all — the rest
        is just time on the clock.

    

    

      
Local-first, by design

      
No central server, no account, no copy on our side to leak, sell or
        hand over. The agent runs on your hardware, on your phone if you
        want it to. The
        manifesto was written
        in April 2026, before the rest was built on top of it.

// INSTALL · on this very machine

  
You are here. To run it:

  
The block below is the real install command for the version
    sitting in ~/.daedalus. Click anywhere
    on the block to copy.


  

    Used by this section:
    install.sh · the installer
    cli_agent_setup_mixin · first-run wizard
    doctor.py · verify the install
    env_loader · read .env safely
  


  
# you are already in this directory, but for reference:
cd ~/.daedalus

# one-shot: installs nothing, just runs
./install.sh --run

# or persistent: registers the `daedalus` command
./install.sh

# or editable .venv (recommended for development)
./install.sh --dev

# or with extras: messaging, cron, mcp
./install.sh --extras "messaging,cron,mcp"

# first run — interactive wizard
daedalus setup

# verify the install
daedalus doctor

# go
daedalus

# config lives at ~/.daedalus/config.yaml
# state lives at ~/.daedalus/state.db
# skills at ~/.daedalus/skills/  (curated, not accumulated)
# sessions, checkpoints, logs all under ~/.daedalus/


  
Verify before claiming. Run daedalus
    doctor to confirm the model endpoint, the memory backend, the
    gateway, the cron scheduler, and the channels. The CLI prints what it
    found, what it expected, and what it did not — not a happy-bot greeting.
